Resolves #6038

Replaces the direct `background-color` and `color` declarations on `.neo-github` in `resources/scss/src/apps/portal/home/parts/hero/Content.scss` with `--button-secondary-background-color` and `--button-secondary-text-color` overrides (`#issuecomment-6656143494`). Previously, `.portal-home-hero-content.neo-container .neo-github` (`(0, 3, 0)` specificity, later source order) shadowed `.neo-button.neo-button-secondary:hover` (`(0, 3, 0)` specificity in `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss`), preventing the secondary button hover state from applying.

`agent-preflight`: not hosted here; baseline `check-engine-brain-boundary`, `test-unit` ran (`restoration` → `fix`).

Evidence: L2 (unit spec in `test/playwright/unit/apps/portal/view/home/ContentBox.spec.mjs` verifying `.neo-github` secondary button config and SCSS variable parameterization without direct `background-color` override) → L2 required (no structured ACs on #6038).

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical. One SCSS block swaps two property declarations for the button's own variables, and a regression test is added. It teaches no architectural concept.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** At `6224370c62`, `.neo-github` now sets `--button-secondary-background-color` and `--button-secondary-text-color` instead of `background-color` and `color`. Both variables exist and are read by the theme (`resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss:236` and `:254`). The unit spec reads the SCSS as text, so I checked the behaviour myself on neomjs.com's production stylesheet, with this PR's exact change applied to the live rule through the CSSOM:

| State | Background | Label |
|---|---|---|
| rest, before and after | `rgb(41, 45, 40)` | `rgb(240, 242, 240)` |
| hover, before | `rgb(41, 45, 40)` (no change) | `rgb(240, 242, 240)` |
| hover, after | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05)` (the theme's secondary hover) | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` |

The resting look is unchanged, and the hover now applies. I looked for a visible side effect and found none. The anchor's own `color` now falls back to the browser's link colour, but nothing visible reads it: the label takes its colour from `.neo-button-text` through the variable, and the button has no glyph element. One non-blocking note: the spec's `toContain` strings include the exact alignment spaces, so a reformat of that block fails the test without a behaviour change.

**Findings:** None.
